title: Sprint-to-Value Microdeck: Engineered Proofs & Seller Scripts — draft
content:
Audience: SEs and platform sellers running fast technical conversations (15–30m) with engineering buyers.

Deck objective: Give sellers a compact set of reproducible, engineer-focused proofs and scripts that convert a skeptical integration architect into a short pilot (mini-POC) within one week. Not a full playbook — think: lab-ready evidence + spoken lines.

Slide 1 — Hook (15s opener)
- 3-line opener: "We help teams get predictable LLM inference at scale — fewer surprises on latency, cost, and capacity. In practice: you can run an embed+chat route with 95th percentile latency under X ms and per-1k-token cost at Y with caching and microbatching."
- Quick tangible: "We can stage a micro-POC in your infra in 48–72 hours."

Slide 2 — What we mean by "engineered proof"
- Short, repeatable checks we bring to every early conversation: latency profile, 95th p95 tail for your seq length, per-inference cost using microbatching, and a simple correctness gate (sample eval set).
- Deliverable: a 2-page evidence sheet + short runbook (we hand to your engineer)

Slide 3 — Fast conversion flow (seller script)
- 0–3 mins: confirm constraints (latency SLO? token/second throughput? regulatory need?) — ask these 3: peak qps, expected seq lengths, private data requirement.
- 3–10 mins: propose micro-POC scope: 1 route, 1 model flavor (quantized if OK), 2 workload patterns (burst vs steady).
- Closing line: "If we can show X latency and Y token cost on your sample within 72 hours, do you want us to build that proof inside your staging VPC or with a redwood sandbox?"

Slide 4 — Evidence examples (engineer-friendly)
- Latency sketch: sample 1: 512 tokens, gpt-family-like, p95=210ms on rdedicated-1 (8xA100); with KV caching cold p95=380ms.
- Cost sketch: naive token cost baseline vs with caching & microbatching: 1M tokens baseline $Z -> optimized pipeline $Z*0.36.
- Accuracy gate: mini-eval of 50 prompts (domain specific) measured by exact-match & human spot-check: target >= 90% pass rate.

Slide 5 — Technical handoff checklist (one-pager text to drop in Slack/email)
- Access: staging AWS role or IP allowlist for 72h, sample corpus (20–100 items), expected query distribution, target SLO, list of forbidden data types.
- Quick command list (for SRE/infra): cURL examples to run sample payloads, simple load script URL, and where to upload logs. (TODO: inline curl snippets — Lina to add)

Slide 6 — Rapid economics worked example (seller-ready)
- Scenario: search+summarize feature, 100k daily queries, avg 600 tokens per session (including context).
- Baseline: non-optimized direct-host = $A/day; with Redwood suggestions (3x microbatching, prefix cache, quantize to 4-bit) -> $A * 0.42/day.
- Seller line: "This is why customers typically pay for Redwood in 2–6 months via saved infra and simpler ops."

Slide 7 — Live roleplay snippets (obs/response)
- Objection: "We already have endpoints; why migrate?"
  - Reply: "Good — this POC is designed to plug into your existing endpoints and surface a delta: reduced cost per inference and a clear tail-latency graph. We'll show you the before/after in a shared dashboard in under a week."
- Objection: "We can't expose data to third-party cloud."
  - Reply: "We can run this inside your VPC or with our private bundle; we only need a short-term staging role and network egress configs for 48–72h. We mirror your audit checklist during the run."

Slide 8 — Quick integration diagram (verbal notes)
- Minimal topology: app -> Redwood inference pool (dedicated) with optional prefix cache -> metrics sink (Prometheus) -> per-route dashboard.
- Talking point: "This diagram is intentionally tiny — for the micro-POC we strip telemetry to the essentials: latency histogram, token counts, error rates."

Slide 9 — Test kit (what we ask engineering to share)
- 20–100 sample queries representative of worst-case and average-case
- 3 typical client app traces or synthetic sequence length distribution
- Acceptable fail criteria (p95 > target or accuracy < threshold)

Slide 10 — Play-by-play timeline (72h staged)
- Day 0: kickoff, access granted, sample data shared
- Day 1: ingest + baseline runs; first latency and cost snapshot
- Day 2: apply optimization knobs (batching, cache, quant), run A/B, produce artifact pack
- Day 3: review meeting (30m) with dashboard and short decision options (expand, tune, or stop)

Appendix A — Seller crib notes (short)
- Two fastest intros: "We’re here to prove economics and operational predictability, not to replace your model stack." and "We’ll hand you a one-page evidence sheet you can show your CTO."
- Three quick metrics to show execs: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, predicted monthly bill delta.

Appendix B — Example evidence sheet (text summary)
- Baseline run (no optim): p95=420ms; optimized run: p95=190ms; token cost baseline: $0.018/token -> optimized token cost: $0.0065/token; expected monthly savings: 42%.
- Notes: numbers illustrative — must be re-run on customer sample.

Author notes / TODOs
- Add cURL & load test snippets (Lina)
- Add quick Prom dashboard template (Jonah)
- Validate economic multipliers for various model sizes (Ethan)
- Capture two short customer anecdotes from CS: near-term wins where we cut ops cost by more than half (ask CS for case IDs)

Roughness intentionally: this is a sprint artifact to be refined in two hours of SE pairing. Use it as a living slide deck — drop in real numbers when you have the sample trace.

Quick links / references (for seller prep)
- Confluence proof template: CONFLUENCE-1234
- SE enablement repo (snippet deck): git.redwood/example-quick-deck (placeholder)

End notes: want to avoid large slides. Keep each slide maximal 6 bullets and always bring a one-pager evidence sheet. If customer asks for deeper bench, escalate to solutions-eng with ticket key: JIRA-GTM-987.
